summary: Multivocal literature review (search Jan 2026) of 31 peer-reviewed papers and 73 quality-screened grey sources on how LLM-assisted coding creates technical debt, mapped onto Alves et al.'s 13 debt types. It adds LLM-specific categories (prompt, fast-integration, governance, provenance, ethical, data debt) and catalogs mitigation strategies, tools such as SonarQube/Snyk/CodeSmellEval, and the absence of LLM-specific benchmarks and metrics.

claims.claim: LLMs amplify traditional code, design and documentation debt most.
claims.evidence: §4.1 frequency counts across grey and formal sources, Fig. 5; counts reflect how often sources discuss a debt type, not measured incidence.

claims.claim: Fast-integration debt triggers a domino effect into governance debt and higher long-term maintenance costs.
claims.evidence: §4.1.1: governance debt in 19 grey sources, fast-integration in 13; the causal chain is the authors' synthesis of practitioner opinion with no longitudinal or quantitative evidence (§5.1 itself calls for longitudinal studies).

claims.claim: No standardized benchmarks or LLM-specific technical debt metrics exist.
claims.evidence: §4.4–4.5, §5.4 across both literatures; plausible given the corpus, but peer-reviewed-only inclusion excludes arXiv preprints, where much of this work appears.

claims.claim: SonarQube is the commonly used tool for detecting debt indicators in LLM code.
claims.evidence: §4.3.1 grey sources; several supporting sources are vendor blogs (Sonar 2025, Codescene, Qodo, Armorcode, Cast) among the 38 company-blog sources.

patterns.note: Static analysis (SonarQube, Snyk) is the dominant practitioner mitigation, but the paper argues such tools are not designed for LLM-specific debt; no effectiveness evidence.
Human-in-the-loop review is the most cited strategy; based on opinion counts, not outcome data.
Recommends tracking/versioning prompts alongside code and documenting AI involvement for provenance.

methodology.sample: 551 formal papers screened to 31 (ACM, IEEE, Springer, Elsevier); 132 grey sources from first 10 Google pages screened to 73 via a 22-criterion checklist (>11 threshold)
methodology.variance: Cohen's kappa 0.93 for debt types on formal sources, 0.90–1.00 elsewhere; grey QA 'agreement 1.0' is post-reconciliation consensus, not IRR

standards.artifacts: Supplementary annotation sheets and assessments on figshare
standards.preregistration: No protocol registration reported; follows Garousi and Kitchenham guidelines

biases.detail: Formal corpus restricted to peer-reviewed venues, excluding arXiv where most 2025 LLM/agent SE work appears; grey corpus limited to first 10 Google pages.
Findings count opinions in sources; 38 of 73 grey sources are company blogs, several from quality-tool vendors promoting their own tools.
New 'debt' labels (fast-integration, governance) rename known review and process concerns without operational definitions or measurement.
Framed around LLM-generated code and assistants; autonomous coding-agent workflows appear only incidentally.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None evaluated; commercial tools are cataloged
coi.detail: Academic authors; the vendor tilt comes from grey sources, not authors.

verdict_reason: Methodical, peer-reviewed (TOSEM) review with QA and kappa, useful as a vocabulary and gap map. Its central causal claims come from practitioner opinion, a large share of grey sources are vendor blogs, and excluding preprints leaves the agentic literature largely out.
applicability: Mostly a framing aid for the team's governance design. Practical takeaways: treat prompts, rules and specs as versioned artifacts. Spec-driven development already does this; extend it to agent rule files and skill prompts across all several repositories. Record provenance of agent-authored changes (which host and model, which spec) for domain data where auditability matters. Keep a local Sonar/static-analysis gate, but do not expect it to catch LLM-specific debt such as duplicated near-identical ingestion adapters across repos. The paper offers no Java- or multi-repo-specific evidence and no measured effect sizes.

conflicts_with.detail: Complementary taxonomy: that mapping extends AI technical debt to agentic systems (memory, orchestration, multi-agent), which this review largely leaves out by excluding preprints and focusing on generated code.
